leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eight round-1 files prefer a single-part prize for optical lattice clocks to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. What is shared: the magic-wavelength lattice as the original idea, the roughly 1e-18 performance as the decisive demonstration, independent reproduction across national laboratories, and a two-name credit. What is not shared: the citation wording (some stress invention and realisation, some the 10^-18 level, some the lattice trap itself), how much weight to give the foundational uses (constants, redshift) versus capability, and the ranking among fallback options (B010, B034, B036, B032 appear as alternatives). Three of the seven (Danielsson, Mehlig, Johansson) moved to B004 from other opening first choices or lower ranks, and each says the count alone is not the argument. Every one of the seven lists the same overlap and attribution reservations.

One member prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene to Allan H. MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Rafi Bistritzer, built on the theory-then-experiment structure (the 2011 flat-band prediction and the 2018 correlated and superconducting phases) and its follow-on from the 2010 graphene prize. He himself concedes the field is about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and Yuan Cao and earlier moire band-structure theorists are outside the trio, and says a maturity-first reading could put B004 ahead. B010 is named as an alternative by Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson, who treat it as a candidate for a later cycle or as a fallback, not as a current first choice.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members regard the optical lattice clock work (B004) as scientifically strong: an original idea (magic-wavelength trapping that removes Doppler, recoil and light-shift limits), a decisive demonstration at the 1e-18 level, and independent reproduction at several national laboratories and in intercontinental comparisons. Even the one dissenter on the configuration, Eriksson, calls B004 the stronger mature choice if the overlap question is settled.

Seven members propose the same credited pair, Katori and Ye, with the same division of roles: Katori for the proposal and first strontium lattice clock, Ye for the accuracy records and the many-body Fermi-degenerate clock. No file proposes a different set of names for B004.

All seven B004 supporters name the same strongest reservation, namely overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems and ion clocks, and all say the wording of the citation will decide whether that overlap matters.
Members agree the redefinition of the SI second has not yet taken place, so part of the practical payoff is still prospective.
Members agree that a prize for B010 would need to be worded around flat bands and correlated phases, not the pairing mechanism, and that Yuan Cao's omission is a real attribution problem.
scientific_disputes: Whether B004 is a new regime of measurement that tests nature (constancy of constants, millimetre-scale gravitational redshift) or primarily an instrument and metrology achievement. Danielsson and Lindroth each say the constants tests so far give null results and prefer to justify the award by capability; Johansson, Mehlig and Pearce lean on the foundational uses. Lindroth and Mehlig also note that a prize for a measurement tool is less of a surprise in nature than a new phase or a new observational window.

Whether a prize can be defended without a settled mechanism for the new phases, which is what the B010 case depends on; Eriksson says it can, Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson treat it as a reason to wait.

Whether the physics in B004 is mainly a refinement of established precision spectroscopy or a separable invention. Danielsson argues that the comb counts optical cycles and does not contain the idea of trapping neutral atoms at a magic wavelength; Mehlig and Kroll still see risk of a continuation reading.
attribution_disputes: For B004, whether Katori's magic-wavelength proposal or the first operational lattice clock marks the original contribution (raised by Olsson and Pearce), and whether Lemonde, Takamoto, Hinkley, Ludlow, Oates and the SYRTE group should be credited. All seven supporters keep to two names; none has shown why the third seat is unnecessary or what it would add.
Ye's name recurs in other candidacies (flagged by Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce), and it is not agreed whether that bears on a single-prize configuration.

For B010, Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, is outside the credited trio, and Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto and Suarez Morell on the earlier moire band-structure side are not captured. Eriksson, Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson all flag the Cao issue.
For B032 (named as an alternative by Danielsson and Pearce), Halzen and Karle lead a collaboration of hundreds and Yoshida's place in the credited set is questioned in Danielsson's response.
maturity_disputes: Whether the pending redefinition of the SI second should come first (Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce each raise it) or whether performance already justifies the award; Olsson adds that the redefinition could sharpen the citation.
Whether B010 is mature at about eight years with open pairing physics (Eriksson, Danielsson, Mehlig); no member argues that the field is fully settled.

Whether B032 is mature given that the diffuse flux is firm while individual source associations remain at modest significance and KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD are only partly independent confirmations (Pearce, Danielsson).
Whether circuit QED (B034) leaves room after the 2025 prize (Johansson, Olsson); this is raised as a question and not asserted by anyone as settled.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, superconducting circuits, Chalmers) flags a possible conflict on B034 circuit QED and B043 optomechanics, would step back from advocating them and would recuse if the committee requires.

Kroll discloses a mild institutional overlap with B034 and other quantum-technology candidates through the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology management team, and a company role at Deep Light Vision AB with an atomic-physics and rare-earth quantum-memory background adjacent to B004, B036 and B013, with no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye.

Pearce (chair) flags field proximity to B032 IceCube (same astroparticle community; collaborations are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, not IceCube) and is not recommending it as the preferred prize.

Danielsson discloses cosmology familiarity regarding B045, his opening top choice, and treats it as a bias to discount; Eriksson notes only a field-proximity interest in B027 (DFT+DMFT) and is not preferring it.

Olsson and Mehlig note that Johansson and Olsson are Chalmers colleagues and that Mehlig is in the neighbouring GU department; neither treats this as a recusal matter. No member discloses a conflict with Katori or Ye.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee accept that optical lattice clocks (B004) are distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes? If so, which citation wording makes the magic-wavelength lattice itself the subject, as Danielsson asked, and who on the committee can state that distinction in terms Eriksson, who defers to AMO colleagues, can evaluate?

Is a two-name prize (Katori and Ye) defensible given Lemonde, Takamoto, Hinkley, Ludlow, Oates and the SYRTE group? Can any member show a specific decisive contribution that would justify a third name, or state why the record supports exactly two?

Should the committee wait for the SI second redefinition, or is the measured 1e-18 performance and its reproduction sufficient now? Is the argument for B004 primarily capability or fundamental physics, given the constants tests have so far given null results?

Should this be a single-part prize, or is there a defensible second part (B010, B032, B036, B034 are named as alternatives)? If a second part is proposed, which member will present its case, with what laureates, and how does that change the credit coherence that Kroll values in the single-topic prize?

For B010, what must be true on attribution (the omission of Yuan Cao and earlier moire band-structure theorists) and on maturity (open pairing mechanism) for it to rank above or beside B004, and can Eriksson say whether he keeps B010 first if the overlap question for B004 is resolved in B004's favour?
Given that Ye appears in other candidacies and Johansson has flagged B034 and B043, does the committee want any formal recusal or step-back recorded before the final ballot, and for which ballot IDs?
summary.chair_observation: The first round is more converged than diverse: seven of eight files prefer B004 with the same two names, and one prefers B010. Several of the seven reached B004 by changing their opening positions (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig) after reading colleagues' ballots, so round 2 should test the scientific argument itself and not take the count as evidence. The unresolved issues are overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes, whether two names fairly cover the record, and the timing of the SI second redefinition. No member has proposed a multi-part configuration as their preferred outcome, so round 2 should decide whether a second part is worth discussing at all.
